title: Answer keys and test answers
unavailable.title: Not available here
forbidden.title: Only people who can edit the course see answer keys
forbidden.body: Answer keys and test answers reveal the answers, so owners, admins and authors see them here.
intro: Each question's answer key decides what counts as right. Test answers are answers you know a question must reject (a likely mistake) or accept. Keys change only on a draft, and every change is checked against the test answers first.
releaseHint: Choose a draft to change keys and rubrics. Published releases can be tested but never change.
releaseOption: Version {version} ({state, select, draft {draft} pending_review {in review} approved {approved} published {published} archived {archived} other {{state}}})
readOnly: This release is published, so its keys and rubrics stay as they are. To change one, create a draft of the next version in Course and releases, then choose it here.
run.title: Test run
run.body: Grades every test answer against the chosen release's keys, the same way learners' answers are graded. Code and written answers are not run here.
run.failedTitle: {count, plural, one {# test answer failed} other {# test answers failed}}
run.failedLine: {item} · {label}: should be {expected, select, correct {accepted} other {rejected}}, was graded {outcome, select, correct {right} incorrect {wrong} invalid_answer {as an answer that does not fit the question} item_missing {without the question (it is not in this release)} other {{outcome}}}
run.allPassed: Every test answer was graded as expected.
courseRubric: Graded against the course rubric “{rubric}”, edited below.
notEditable: An installed evaluator grades this question (for example code with hidden test cases). Its key is not edited here.
key.toleranceHint: How far an answer may be from the right value and still count.
key.unitHint: Optional. When set, an answer in another unit is sent back, not marked wrong.
key.explanationHint: Required. Learners see it after they answer.
key.checkFirst: Check the change against the test answers before saving.
key.saved: Key saved to the draft. The draft needs review again before it is published.
key.acceptFailing: Save anyway: {count, plural, one {# test answer} other {# test answers}} will be graded the wrong way
impact.none: This question has no test answers yet. Add some below so changes can be checked.
impact.summary: With this key: {failing, plural, =0 {every test answer is graded as expected} one {# test answer would be graded the wrong way} other {# test answers would be graded the wrong way}} · {changed, plural, =0 {no result changes} one {# result changes} other {# results change}}.
impact.line: should be {expected, select, correct {accepted} other {rejected}}, would be graded {outcome, select, correct {right} incorrect {wrong} invalid_answer {as not fitting} other {{outcome}}}
fixtures.label: Test answers
fixtures.title: Test answers ({count})
fixtures.hint: Add answers this question must reject, such as a likely mistake, and answers it must accept.
fixtures.notRunnable: Test answers for code and written questions are not run here: code needs the sandbox evaluator and written answers a reviewer.
fixtures.unitHint: Optional, as a learner could type it.
fixtures.labelHint: Optional, for example the mistake it stands for.
fixtures.addedPassed: Added. The current key already grades it as expected.
fixtures.addedFailed: Added, but the current key grades it the wrong way ({outcome, select, correct {right} incorrect {wrong} other {{outcome}}}). Fix the key on a draft.
rubric.eyebrow: Course rubric · version {version} · used by {count, plural, one {# question} other {# questions}}
rubric.versionHint: Changed criteria need a new version, for example 1.1.0, so earlier reviews keep pointing at the rubric they used.
